user.title: Haier HWHP – connection
user.description: Connection details for the Modbus TCP interface. The HWHP's native interface is Modbus RTU (9600 8N1), so the host is usually a Modbus RTU-to-TCP converter (gateway).

data_description.host: Usually the IP of the Modbus RTU-to-TCP converter, not the heat pump itself.
data_description.slave: Modbus address of the heat pump on the RTU bus (default 1).

cop.title: Haier HWHP – COP & energy
cop.description: COP = produced heat / electricity used. Leave a meter empty to use the device's integrated Modbus register; pick an entity to use an external meter. Tip: for an external electricity meter, pick a yearly-resetting counter (utility_meter, cycle: yearly) so the window matches the device's yearly heat total. Changeable later via "Configure".

data.cop_elec_entity: External electricity meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_heat_entity: External heat meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_ref_date: COP reference date (empty = auto; day the heat counter was reset)

pv.title: Haier HWHP – PV mode
pv.description: Optional PV-surplus control. Pick the operating mode: Off (only the raw entities + 38 °C guard), Coordinator (the integration controls the setpoint itself from the raw PV surplus + a fixed morning start), or Executor (an external HEMS controls it via select.haier_hwhp_pv_program). The next page shows exactly the fields for the chosen mode. Changeable later via "Configure".

data_description.pv_mode: Off: the integration does not regulate (only the raw entities + 38 °C guard). Coordinator: the integration controls the setpoint from the raw PV surplus — fixed morning start, raise to the elevated target only while the heat pump already runs (piggyback), plus an ad-hoc electric-heater tier above the high threshold. Executor: an external HEMS controls it via the pv_program select; the integration only provides the programs.

pv_details.title: Haier HWHP – PV settings
pv_details.description: Settings for the selected PV mode. Coordinator: surplus sensor, target temps and the control thresholds. Executor: only the target temps (the mechanic for the program select).

data_description.pv_sensor: Raw PV surplus in W (≥ 0). Required for Coordinator mode.
data_description.pv_hold: Buffer above which the heat-pump cycle is raised to and held at the elevated target — but the daytime raise happens only while the pump already runs (piggyback), so no extra cold starts. Drops back to normal after the debounce time once surplus stays below this and the heater is off.
data_description.pv_solar_boost: Threshold above which the heat-pump cycle (while already running, piggyback) keeps climbing on its own up to the boost target — via the compressor alone, far more efficient (COP typically 3–4x) than the electric heater. Must sit between the hold/piggyback threshold and the heater threshold. No universal spec value exists — best derived from your own external power meter (e.g. Shelly, see COP electricity source): read the compressor's typical draw and set this just above it.
data_description.pv_high: Electric-heater threshold (≈ 1550 W = heater ~1500 W + buffer). Above it the heater is added as an ad-hoc top-up at the boost target: Boost while the heat pump runs, ELEC only while it is off. The heater never stops the pump — when surplus drops, only the heater goes away while the cycle keeps running.
data_description.pv_morning_time: Once per day at this time, if the water is below the normal target, kick the setpoint to the elevated target so the heat pump starts within the device ECO window.
data_description.pv_min_off: Anti-short-cycle for the morning start: a fresh cold start waits until the compressor has been off at least this long. Daytime raises happen only while the pump already runs (piggyback) and are unaffected.
data_description.pv_escalation: What to add once surplus passes the high threshold — an ad-hoc heater top-up that never stops the heat-pump cycle. None: just the higher setpoint. Boost: heat pump + electric heater together, only while the pump runs (efficient). Electric heater only (ELEC): heater on while the pump is off (it would otherwise stop the pump) — inefficient, only to dump surplus, e.g. after the daily cycle. Back to ECO + normal target once surplus is gone.
data_description.pv_negative_price_sensor: Optional binary_sensor/input_boolean flagging the current quarter-hour as negative/zero-price (e.g. your own template built on Tibber/aWATTar/Nordpool — this integration doesn't compute the price itself). When 'on', the electric heater (Boost) may switch on even before the heat pump has reached the Solar-Boost tier — feed-in would be worthless in that window anyway (German 'Solarspitzengesetz'/§51 EEG). Leave empty if you don't have such a sensor (default behaviour is unchanged).

init.description: Connection, COP/energy sources and optional PV surplus control. Host/port/slave change the link to the Modbus converter.

data.cop_elec_entity: External electricity meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_heat_entity: External heat meter (kWh) — empty = Modbus register
data.cop_ref_date: COP reference date (empty = auto; day the heat counter was reset)
data.legionella_interval_days: Interval – max. days without a full heat-up

data_description.pv_mode: Off: the integration does not regulate (only the raw entities + 38 °C guard). Coordinator: the integration controls the setpoint from the raw PV surplus — fixed morning start, raise to the elevated target only while the heat pump already runs (piggyback), plus an ad-hoc electric-heater tier above the high threshold. Executor: an external HEMS controls it via the pv_program select; the integration only provides the programs. The next page shows the fields for the chosen mode (skipped for Off).
data_description.emergency_enabled: When the water gets critically cold, temporarily switches ECO→AUTO to heat immediately (even outside the ECO time window); back to ECO on recovery.
data_description.emergency_critical: Below this water temperature it switches from ECO to AUTO.
data_description.emergency_recover: At/above this water temperature it switches back to ECO.
data_description.legionella_enabled: Forces a thermal disinfection at least every X days: heats the tank to the target until the bottom (tank bottom) holds the verification threshold for the hold time. If the tank gets fully heated anyway in between (e.g. PV boost), that counts and the timer resets. Scald risk: with 65 °C use a thermostatic mixing valve.
data_description.legionella_interval_days: A run is triggered after at most this many days without a verified full heat-up (DVGW practice: 7).
data_description.legionella_bottom_min: The run only counts as reached once the tank bottom – the coldest layer – holds this temperature (slightly below the setpoint).
data_description.legionella_hold_min: How long the tank bottom must hold the verification threshold before the run counts as successful.
data_description.legionella_window_start: Preferred time window (usually the device's ECO window): the run starts here if possible and first heats efficiently in ECO; if it can't reach the target it escalates to AUTO. When overdue, protection is forced even outside this window.
data_description.legionella_window_end: End of the preferred window (usually the device's ECO window).
